links.outcome: Systematic bias of chatbot MADRS scores versus clinician ratings after calibration
links.effect: Chatbot interviews systematically yielded higher severity scores than clinician ratings; bias substantially reduced by lightweight post-hoc calibration (no numbers reported in abstract).
links.quote: This bias was substantially reduced through lightweight post-hoc calibration.

links.outcome: Systematic bias in chatbot-derived depression severity scores
links.effect: Lightweight post-hoc calibration substantially reduced the chatbot's systematically higher severity scores relative to clinician ratings. No numerical effect was reported.
links.quote: This bias was substantially reduced through lightweight post-hoc calibration.

links.effect: MADRS-Chat was well accepted by patients and clinicians; quantitative acceptability results were not reported.
links.quote: <italic>MADRS-Chat</italic>  was well accepted by both patients and clinicians, and chatbot-derived scores showed meaningful agreement with human ratings.
